chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: Dr. Holmes's Good Samaritan brass band for children
summary: A wealthy Black benefactor named Holmes outfitted a band, with a director who taught every instrument, giving instruments to those who promised to stay.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: That's right! Anyway, tell me about the Doctor Holmes,
Holmes (10/9) - 12
no relation, who got together and had a brass band. Tell me about that.
A Good Samaritan.
I see.

He was a Good Samaritan. He made his money, he had his money. I don't know anything about him personally, if he was married or single or anything. I never heard anything about a wife, because I wasn't interested -- I wasn't interested in his wife or anything like that, if he had one.

But all I know, he was outfitting a band for children... And grownups! He wanted a band. He wanted a brass band. And he would front us the estimates. And he had a director that could play all of the instruments in the band, and he would teach. He would teach anybody in the band that wanted to learn how to play.
Now, with the kids, he didn't want nobody that could play anything, that could play an instrument. He wanted to start you off fresh. And he would teach you, and you'd come around that way.
But you had to say that you would stay with the band, didn't you, for about a year...
Well, yeah. I mean, you stayed...
You had to promise to stay with the band if they were
Holmes (10/9) - 13
going to teach you.
Everybody promised to stay when they joined. But he would give you your instruments while you were with the band.
Now, do you remember the name of the fellow who could play all the instruments and who gave tuition? Who taught?
Mmm, he was an Italian. Right now I can't remember his name.
Dr. Holmes was White?
No, no.
He was Black?
He was Black.
